Subject: HealthSys — security exhibit: SOC 2 evidence and pen-test window

Hi Karthik,

We are starting the legal review for the MSA/Order Form and need to align on the security exhibit. A few specific asks from our side:
- Confirm scope of SOC 2 attestation and provide the latest report (Type II preferred).
- We want to run a 2-week penetration test in Q3; please confirm staging access, notice expectations, and what can be in scope.
- For evidence delivery, our compliance team prefers a weekly sprint handoff (artifacts grouped by control families) over a 6-week period so we can validate incrementally.

Can you propose a concise evidence delivery plan, list owners on your side for each artifact family, and flag any audit / pen-test language that Redwood will not accept or needs to be limited?

Also looping in Procurement (Tom Lee) for timing constraints.

Thanks,
Claire W.
Security & Compliance, HealthSys

Subject: Re: HealthSys — security exhibit: SOC 2 evidence and pen-test window

Claire — thanks for the clear asks. High level proposal from Redwood: 3-phase, timeboxed approach that meets your weekly sprint preference while protecting operational safety and tenant isolation. Details below.

Phase 1 — Attestation drop (Day 0):
- We will provide the latest SOC 2 Type II report (SOC2-report-2025.pdf) plus a short control-mapping spreadsheet.
- Owner: Karthik (legal/assurance liaison) + Laura (contracts).

Phase 2 — Evidence sprints (Weeks 1–6):
- Weekly deliveries grouped by control family (e.g., access controls, change management, incident mgmt). Each delivery includes a stubbed artifact manifest and a small sample set for verification.
- Evidence owners: Laura Bennett (Evidence Ops) for operational artifacts; Marissa Cole (Engineering liaison) for staging/access details.
- We will publish artifacts to a shared Drive folder and notify your team with sprint notes. See draft playbook attached (evidence-playbook-v1.md).

Phase 3 — Pen-test notice & window (Q3, 2-week window):
- Redwood accepts a mutually agreed 2-week pen-test window on non-production/staging systems only. Requirements we need in contract language: 48-hour advance formal notice; timeboxed to agreed dates; scope limited to redacted sample targets and must not include production; test must be coordinated with Redwood on-call.

Contract/Order Form redlines we will ask Legal to propose:
- Limit inspection/penetration testing to non-prod with explicit notice and coordination.
- Require mutually agreeable third-party testers or explicit vendor qualifications.
- Define sampling size for evidence (we propose sample sets of up to 5 instances per control family; this reduces blast risk).

I expect Laura will push a tracked redline for the Audit Rights / Security Exhibit sections. Attaching the draft playbook and will follow up with a tracked MSA redline.

Next steps: Laura to circulate redlines; I'll sync with Marissa on operational runbook.

— Karthik
Head, Enterprise Accounts — Redwood Inference

Claire / Karthik — Laura here (Legal). Appreciate the clear framing. I attached a tracked redline of the MSA Security Exhibit (MSA_redline_track_changes.docx) with the key contract positions distilled below. High-level summary of proposed language changes: 

1) Audit / Inspection Rights 
- We propose language to constrain "inspection" and "pen-test" to non-production environments only and to require a minimum 48-hour formal notice plus a mutually agreed test plan.
- Redwood requests removal of unconstrained continuous inspection clauses; instead we accept quarterly attestation and timeboxed inspection rights tied to specific audit requests.

2) Penetration Testing
- Redwood will permit third-party testing subject to tester qualification, a predefined scope document, and an execution window that is scheduled at least two weeks in advance; Redwood reserves right to limit tests that could impact multi-tenant isolation.

3) Evidence Delivery Cadence
- We accept weekly evidence handoffs but will map artifacts to specific SOC 2 control IDs and agree on sampling methodology (recommended: sample size N=5 per control family). All artifacts will be redacted to remove PII/ customer-specific content.

4) Data Access and Redaction
- Any on-demand access to logs or telemetry is subject to a redaction / minimization step and must be retrieved via a formal request channel; we will not provide full tenant-level exports.

5) Escalation / SLA carveouts
- For emergency responses requiring deeper access, Redwood will provide an exception process with an exec-level approval path rather than open access.

I've included inline edits to the exhibit; Marissa, please review the operational statements about staging access and sample sets so we can align the playbook language with legal redlines. Claire — once you review the redline, let us know which items are non-starters for HealthSys and we can iterate.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachments: MSA_redline_track_changes.docx

Thanks — Laura and Karthik, this is helpful and aligned with our expectations. A few quick confirmations and requests: 

- SOC2 report: excellent, we received SOC2-report-2025.pdf. We'll include that as the primary attestation.
- Pen-test window: we can accept non-prod only. We will add one week of prep before the 2-week testing window (so 3 calendar weeks total). Are you ok with that?
- Evidence cadence: weekly handoffs look good; one ask — please add a short "artifact acceptance checklist" per sprint so our reviewers have a consistent validation template.

Procurement (Tom) asked that we get the redline back into DocuSign by Aug 6 to keep procurement timelines; is that possible from your side? We'll also upload completed sprint artifacts to your Drive folder.

Next steps:
- Karthik / Laura: finalize redline and propose a DocuSign send date (targeting Aug 3 from Redwood).
- Marissa: please confirm the Evidence Ops owner(s) and add the artifact acceptance checklist to the next playbook revision.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Claire W.
Security & Compliance, HealthSys
